facts.statement: The only known species of the genus Choyrodon is Choyrodon barsboldi.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Choyrodon barsboldi.

facts.statement: The genus name Choyrodon combines the Mongolian city of Choyr with the Latin word for tooth.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the city of Choyr, and -odon, from Latin for tooth

facts.statement: The species name barsboldi honors the Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold.
facts.quote: the specific name barsboldi honours paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold.

facts.statement: American paleontologist Terry Gates and colleagues formally named Choyrodon barsboldi in 2018.
facts.quote: in 2018 American paleontologist Terry Gates and colleagues named them Choyrodon barsboldi.

facts.statement: Three distinct specimens of Choyrodon have been found in the lower member of the Khuren Dukh Formation.
facts.quote: Three specimens of Choyrodon are known, each from a different locality of the lower member of the Khuren Dukh Formation.

facts.statement: Choyrodon lived during the Early Cretaceous (Albian) in the Khuren Dukh Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: Choyrodon is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian) Khuren Dukh Formation of Mongolia.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis identifies Choyrodon as the sister taxon of Eolambia.
facts.quote: It was found to be the sister taxon of Eolambia.

facts.statement: Choyrodon is distinguished from the coexisting Altirhinus by the presence of an open antorbital fenestra.
facts.quote: Choyrodon displays an open antorbital fenestra, which clearly distinguishes it from coexisting Altirhinus

facts.statement: Researchers found no evidence to support the hypothesis that Choyrodon is a juvenile form of Altirhinus.
facts.quote: There was not support for interpreting Choyrodon as a juvenile Altirhinus, despite their similar anatomy, age, and location.

facts.statement: Choyrodon is classified within the infraorder Ornithopoda.
Choyrodon belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
Choyrodon lived approximately 110 to 100 million years ago during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 110 y 100 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Choyrodon spans from 110.1 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPC-D 100/801 was discovered in the lower deposits of the Choeren Doe formation dating to the middle Albian.
facts.quote: El holotipo , MPC-D 100/801, se encontró en el depósito inferior de la formación Choeren Doe, que data de mediados de Albiense.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton including a skull, lower jaws, cervical ribs, and metacarpals.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial con cráneo, mandíbulas inferiores, costillas del cuello y metacarpianos.

facts.statement: The skull features a supraoccipital bone overlapping on both sides, which researchers interpret as an opisthotic bone.
facts.quote: En la parte posterior de la cabeza, el supraoccipital se superpone en ambos lados por un pedazo de pierna que los descriptores interpretan como el opistótico.

facts.statement: While some suggest Choyrodon is merely a juvenile Altirhinus, the describers argue against this based on specific anatomical differences.
facts.quote: Esto sugiere que Choyrodon es solo el cachorro de Altirhinus . Sin embargo, los descriptores dan algunos argumentos sobre por qué este no sería el caso.

facts.statement: Choyrodon retains an antorbital fenestra, a feature absent in the holotype of Altirhinus.
facts.quote: Choyrodon todavía tiene una fenestra antorbital, una característica básica que carece del holotipo de Altirhinus.

facts.statement: Choyrodon is placed as a basal member of Iguanodontia, specifically as the sister species to Eolambia.
facts.quote: Choyrodon se coloca en basal en Iguanodontia como una especie hermana de Eolambia.
